title: Threaded back stitch
subtitle: Back stitch laced with a second thread to add a looped decorative edge
excerpt: Threaded back stitch weaves a second thread through back stitch in a series of loops, alternating above and below each stitch to produce a looped border with a different colour. The lacing thread never enters the fabric.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), composite outline stitches (Project Gutenberg #20776). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), laced back stitch entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: The second thread woven through the foundation stitches from a blunt needle. It creates the decorative loops without entering the fabric surface.

heroPrompt: Threaded back stitch in gold lacing thread over dark blue back stitch on cream linen, showing the looped border on each side, close-up, natural light.

content.text: alternately over and under the foundation back stitches. The lacing thread goes up through the space above one stitch, then down through the space below the next, producing regular loops on both sides of the line.

items.label: Foundation thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 strands in colour A

items.label: Lacing thread
items.value: Stranded cotton or fine ribbon in colour B

items.label: Needles
items.value: Embroidery needle for foundation; blunt tapestry needle for lacing

content.text: Work a line of evenly spaced back stitch with colour A.
Thread the tapestry needle with colour B. Bring it up at the start of the line.
Slide the needle upward through the first back stitch gap, then downward through the second, alternating throughout.
Do not pull the lacing thread tight; allow small loops to form evenly above and below the line.

attrs.heading: When threaded back stitch goes wrong

items.symptom: The loops are uneven in size
items.cause: The foundation back stitches are different lengths.
items.fix: Work the foundation with very regular stitch length. Mark intervals on the transfer line first.

items.symptom: The lacing thread pulls the foundation line out of shape
items.fix: Let the lacing thread lie loosely. It should loop freely above and below the foundation line without tension.

content.text: Threaded back stitch is a straightforward introduction to composite stitches where two threads work together. Pekinese stitch uses a similar lacing action but with a more complex interlocking loop.
